fullPassage: Robert Schumann once said, "The laws of morals are those of art." What the great man is saying here is that there is good music and bad music. The greatest music, even if it's tragic in nature, takes us to a world higher than ours; somehow the beauty uplifts us. Bad music, on the other hand, degrades us. It's the same with performances: a bad performance isn't necessarily the result of incompetence. Some of the worst performances occur when the performers, no matter how accomplished, are thinking more of themselves than of the music they're playing. These doubtful characters aren't really listening to what the composer is saying — they're just showing off, hoping that they'll have a great 'success' with the public. The performer's basic task is to try to understand the meaning of the music, and then to communicate it honestly to others.

det.korean: 빈칸에 communicate it honestly to others가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignore what the composer intended(작곡가 의도 무시): 반대
✅ ② communicate it honestly to others(정직하게 다른 이에게 전달): 연주자의 기본 임무 ← 정답
❌ ③ impress the public with clever tricks(재주로 대중을 감동): 나쁜 연주자의 태도
❌ ④ play the music as loudly as possible(최대한 크게 연주): 본문에 없음
det.tip: basic task: understand the meaning and communicate it honestly
